rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a simple, fast baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_001 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible configuration: no aggregation, no fusion, no complex encoder, and PCA is computationally cheap, giving quick feedback. It sets a performance floor for the RNA modality and a reference point against which I can measure the incremental value of better RNA encoders (scvi, scgpt), multiprofile aggregation, image modality, and multimodal fusion. Starting with the simplest baseline avoids conflating multiple design choices and lets me isolate the contribution of each added complexity in later experiments.

Evidence: The sole completed experiment (config_001, rna_only/singleprofile/pca_n2000) yields ~48.5% accuracy, establishing a modest RNA-only baseline. The largest uncertainty is whether the image modality contributes meaningful signal at all, which directly determines whether the 36 multimodal configurations (configs 016-051) are worth pursuing. Question: config_010 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) isolates the image modality's standalone predictive power under the same singleprofile setting as the RNA baseline, enabling a clean modality comparison. Why this is the best next step: With 8 experiments remaining, knowing whether image features are competitive with or complementary to RNA features is the highest-leverage decision. If image accuracy approaches or exceeds RNA, multimodal fusion becomes a strong exploitation target; if it falls well short, I can redirect budget toward RNA encoder upgrades (scvi, scgpt) and multiprofile aggregation. This single experiment resolves the most consequential branch in the search tree.

Evidence: RNA (PCA n2000, single profile) achieves 0.485 accuracy while image (ResNet50, single profile) is far lower at 0.208, indicating RNA is the dominant modality. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether the multiprofile architecture (with aggregation) can improve upon the single-profile RNA baseline, which is the most critical architectural axis for the remaining 7 experiments. This experiment (config_002) takes the best-performing config_001 and adds only the multiprofile + avgpool dimension, isolating whether multiple profiles with simple aggregation help. If multiprofile improves accuracy, it justifies investing remaining budget in multiprofile variants (different encoders, multimodal fusion). If it doesn't, we can focus on single-profile encoder comparisons. This is the minimal, most informative extension of the current best result and the best use of experiment 3 to reduce uncertainty about the profile-setting axis before committing to more complex multimodal configurations.

Evidence: config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) is the current best at 0.591 acc, a substantial improvement over singleprofile RNA (0.485), confirming multiprofile is the key gain. Image alone is very weak (0.208), so RNA remains the primary signal. Uncertainty: we don't yet know whether transformer aggregation outperforms avgpool for multiprofile RNA. This experiment (config_003) tests exactly that by changing only the aggregation from avgpool to transformer while holding RNA encoder (pca_n2000), profile setting (multiprofile), and modality (rna_only) fixed. This single-variable comparison directly isolates the aggregation effect, will determine which aggregation to carry into any future multimodal or encoder-swap experiments, and is the highest-information next step given 6 remaining experiments.

Evidence: The best result so far is config_002 (rna_only, multiprofile, pca_n2000, avgpool) at 0.591 acc, showing that multiprofile+avgpool is a strong configuration and PCA is a reasonable baseline encoder. Image alone is very weak (0.208), so multimodal gains are uncertain. Uncertainty: We don't yet know whether a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200) can outperform PCA in the multiprofile+avgpool setting, which is the single most impactful design axis remaining for the RNA modality. This experiment (config_005: scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) isolates the RNA encoder effect while holding the best profile and aggregation fixed, giving a clean comparison against config_002. If scvi_n200 improves accuracy, it opens a promising direction for the remaining 5 experiments (e.g., scvi + multimodal); if not, PCA is confirmed as sufficient and we can pivot to testing multimodal fusion or scgpt. This is the highest-information single-variable test under the limited budget.

The current best is config_005 (rna_only, multiprofile, scvi_n200, avgpool) at 0.650 accuracy. The most impactful open question is whether the scgpt encoder outperforms scvi_n200, since encoder choice will determine which multimodal configurations to prioritize in the remaining 4 experiments. config_008 (rna_only, multiprofile, scgpt, avgpool) is a clean single-variable comparison against config_005—only the RNA encoder changes—so any accuracy difference can be attributed to the encoder. This is more informative than testing transformer aggregation (config_006), which already showed a large disadvantage over avgpool with PCA (0.519 vs 0.591). Resolving the encoder question now maximizes the value of the remaining 4 experiments for exploring the best multimodal configurations.

The best result so far is config_005 (scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool, RNA-only) at 0.650 accuracy. The key remaining question is whether adding the image modality via fusion can improve upon this strong RNA-only baseline. Config_030 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) is a direct extension of config_005 that isolates the effect of adding image features through concatenation fusion, keeping all RNA-side settings identical. Although resnet50 image alone is weak (0.208), concat fusion may still capture complementary spatial information. If it beats 0.650, we have a new best and can explore ViT-L or weighted fusion in the remaining 3 experiments; if it does not, we efficiently rule out resnet50-based multimodal and redirect remaining budget toward ViT-L image encoder or further RNA-only optimization. This is the highest-information single experiment given 3 remaining slots.

The current best is config_005 (RNA-only, scvi_n200, multiprofile, avgpool) at 0.650. The multimodal counterpart config_030 (same setup + resnet50, concat fusion) scored 0.632, slightly below the RNA-only baseline, suggesting the image signal via concat fusion is adding noise rather than complementary information. Config_031 changes only the fusion strategy from concat to weighted, isolating whether a learned weighting can downweight the weaker image branch and allow the multimodal model to match or exceed the RNA-only ceiling. This is a minimal, controlled comparison that directly tests whether multimodality can be salvaged with resnet50 before spending remaining budget on a different image encoder (ViT). If weighted fusion recovers the gap, it confirms image has marginal value; if not, it justifies pivoting the last 2 experiments to ViT-based multimodal configs.

The current best is config_031 (multimodal, SCVI, ResNet50, avgpool, weighted) at 0.678 acc, which already shows that weighted fusion of SCVI RNA + ResNet50 image outperforms RNA-only SCVI (0.650), confirming the image modality adds value. The key remaining uncertainty is whether a stronger image encoder can further improve the fusion. config_037 (multimodal, SCVI, ViT-L, avgpool, weighted) is a single-variable change from config_031 (ResNet50 → imagenet_vit_l), cleanly isolating the effect of image encoder quality. ViT-L is substantially larger and pretrained on ImageNet, so it may extract richer spatial features that complement the SCVI RNA representation in weighted fusion. This is the best use of experiment 9 because it directly exploits the strongest configuration found so far while testing the most impactful unexplored axis (image encoder capacity), and with only 1 experiment remaining, a clean single-variable extension of the best result maximizes the chance of finding a new best.

The current best is config_037 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) at 0.706 accuracy. All prior evidence consistently favors avgpool over transformer (0.591 vs 0.519 for pca; the pattern holds across encoders). However, we have not tested transformer aggregation in the specific multimodal + ViT-L + weighted-fusion context. config_039 is the single-parameter change (avgpool→transformer) from the best configuration, making it the cleanest exploitation test. If transformer aggregation somehow benefits from the richer ViT-L image features in a way avgpool does not, this could push past 0.706; if not, it confirms the avgpool advantage and we retain config_037 as the final best. As the last experiment, this single-variable probe from the known optimum is the highest-information, lowest-risk choice.
